findings.minimal_fix: Materialize an exact per-group signed ledger containing source-channel identity plus positive and negative pixel masks, reconcile its positive plus negative population to the independently frozen counts, and translate it into M54 context-valid/context-subtract accepted handshakes.
findings.observation: Canonical M55/M56 count XOR or absolute residual work but do not emit the positive and negative masks required to choose add versus subtract. Independent raw reconstruction finds aggregate dual +422,341,928/-110,379,057 source bits and module-30 dual +46,669,247/-5,397,600; P48 therefore requires +93,338,494/-10,795,200 product updates.

findings.minimal_fix: Freeze a row-bounded P48 schedule with explicit current, left, up and previous-timestep activation reads, parent-choice computation, parent-output seed reads, boundary fallbacks, commit writes, addresses, ports, lifetimes and maximum simultaneous state bytes. Derive all cycles from that ledger.
findings.observation: M56 constructs residuals offline and charges neither parent candidates nor parent-output seeds. A one-bit module-30 prior input timestep is 921,600 bytes, one prior row is 3,840 bytes, one P48 input tile is 576 bytes, and a signed19 two-output prior result frame is 364,800 bytes. M53's 136,800 bytes are two 300x96 signed19 accumulator frames for another schedule and cannot be relabeled as prediction-head parent storage.

findings.minimal_fix: Implement the P48 head adapter in RTL: eight selected source channels per cycle, signed masks for forty-eight pixels, two-weight broadcast, eight-term accumulation into ninety-six pixel-output lanes, union scheduling, tail P32 handling and backpressure. Compare its accepted-handshake ledger against the exact row schedule in VCS before assigning cycle credit.
findings.observation: The P48 arithmetic assumes 8x96=768 product slots per event cycle plus an eight-source reduction for every lane. It has no RTL, SRAM-port, mask-distribution, timing or backpressure proof, and its frozen dual physical-lane utilization is only 25.127%.

findings.minimal_fix: Export the exact float32 weight and bias payload, define and train or calibrate an INT8/fixed-point bridge, prove bit-accurate dense and parent-delta head outputs across valid825, and freeze accuracy before VCS and DC performance work.
findings.observation: The manifest freezes a float32 [2,96,1,1] weight and float32 [2] bias. M56 explicitly assumes resident weights but has neither an INT8 payload nor bias, accumulator-width, numerical-equivalence or accuracy closure.

findings.minimal_fix: Capture and repeat the raw analysis across multiple DSEC sequences and event-density/equal-rate strata using the same checkpoint and module identities.
findings.observation: All ten frozen samples come from the single sequence zurich_city_09_a at sample keys 0001 through 0091; this is full-network depth but not cross-sequence breadth.

findings.minimal_fix: Report per-module and leave-one-head-out ablations and require the improvement to survive at least one independent sequence before treating motion selection as a general full-network mechanism.
findings.observation: Module 30 supplies 28,811,162 of the aggregate 33,996,201 source bits saved by dual versus local, or 84.748181%; the marginal motion advantage is highly concentrated in one terminal head.

findings.minimal_fix: Add choice-generation and metadata bytes to the bounded schedule, including candidate popcounts, tie resolution and per-group parent descriptors; report the traffic separately from source bits.
findings.observation: M55 chooses the minimum parent omnisciently and deliberately excludes metadata/control. A naive two-bit choice record is 177,000,000 bits over all vectors and 15,360,000 bits for module 30, material relative to the corresponding source-bit totals even though the costs are not interchangeable.

findings.minimal_fix: Map the terminal-head schedule into the ordered full-network trace and publish its baseline latency share plus an Amdahl composition; retain P1/P48 and dense/P48 only as head-kernel opportunity ratios until then.
findings.observation: M56 covers one terminal 1x1 two-output head. Its P1/P48 19.052977x grouping ratio and dense/P48 plus-commit 3.086428x ratio do not establish how much end-to-end latency this head occupies.
